parsed.explanation: The dossier documents no trans-specific offence, no universal-exposure measure (no facility, custody, border or screening rule reaching visitors), and no organised targeting of gender-nonconforming people. Decriminalisation came via a 2022 court ruling that also read constitutional sex discrimination to cover gender identity — a functioning-rule-of-law positive. Against this: only a single pre-2022 assault is recorded (weak evidence either way), no trans-specific violence data exists, the government resisted repeal for years, there is no statutory anti-discrimination protection, and no gender-recognition mechanism — a resident-facing gap that signals an institutional climate less trans-affirming than the acceptance-with-protections tier, but which touches visitors only if officials doubt foreign documents, which the dossier does not document. No third-gender tradition or documented social acceptance is recorded, and port-of-entry and custody practice are unresolved open questions. This sits near the 0.65-C anchor: no known visitor-facing exposure, thin formal recourse, latent stigma signals, one step below documented-acceptance jurisdictions.
